text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm updating the minimal "hello app" quickstart to use the new token refresh flow instead of long-lived API keys. Need a docs PR review + updated SDK snippets.

sam: +1, thanks. can you list the exact snippets that change? i can update the JS one.

maya: Sure — two main snippets: 1) auth setup (exchanging refresh token for access token) and 2) the example client init and first deployment command. Also one link in the auth section points to /docs/auth#apikey which should be /docs/auth#token-refresh.

leo: I noticed the quickstart has a tiny deploy command that uses `--model=gpt-3.5` — should we standardize on the catalog name `redwood/gpt-3.5-mini`? that's been the recommended pattern.

maya: Good catch. I'll change model name and the env var names to the new convention (REDWOOD_REFRESH_TOKEN).

tara: For the JS snippet i18n, we should also show the refresh flow with async/await and a short retry example. i can PR that after your draft.

maya: Drafted a PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2439 — contains updated Python and JS snippets, a short paragraph about token lifetime, and the link fix.

docs-bot: Pull request opened by maya: #2439 — CI checks: docs linting ✅, linkcheck flagged 1 broken anchor -> fixed in branch.

sam: Reviewing now. small nits: in JS snippet you're using `RedwoodClient({ apiKey })` — needs to be `RedwoodClient({ accessToken })` after refresh.

maya: Updated. Also added this minimal Python snippet to demonstrate refresh + call:```python
# exchange refresh token for access token
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient, auth
refresh = "${REDWOOD_REFRESH_TOKEN}"
access = auth.exchange_refresh_token(refresh)
client = RedwoodClient(access_token=access)
resp = client.generate("Hello world")
print(resp.text)
```

leo: Nice. Can we add a one-liner showing env var export for dev? e.g. `export REDWOOD_REFRESH_TOKEN=...` and a note about storing refresh tokens in a secrets store.

maya: Done in the PR. Also added a small note: "refresh tokens should be rotated and stored in KMS/secret manager; access tokens are short lived and should not be persisted."

tara: I left comments on the PR about tightening the language in the paragraph that explains when to use Dedicated vs Hosted for token rotation. Might be a bit opinionated.

maya: Thanks, i addressed the wording and added an internal link to the security best-practices doc.

sam: One more thing — the hello app quickstart includes a `start` script with `--port=8080`. Our container infra defaults to 8081 now; can you change that to `PORT` env var and `process.env.PORT || 8081` in examples?

maya: Updated both Python guide (gunicorn bind) and JS example (express listen) to use `PORT` env fallback.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy for docs site triggered by PR #2439 -> staging.redwood.ai/docs — rendered successfully, no visual diffs detected for quickstart page.

leo: Quick manual check on staging looks good. One tiny spacing nit in the code block, i'll mark it in PR.

maya: Addressed spacing, ran linkcheck locally. All links pass.

sam: LGTM from me. Approving the PR.

tara: Approved.

maya: Thanks all — i'll merge after CI green in ~10m and file a follow-up to add a small migration note for customers using API keys.

docs-bot: PR #2439 merged by maya — docs site rebuilt and published.

maya: closing loop — thx for the quick turnaround. leaving a short follow-up ticket to add a migration checklist for self-hosted customers (rotation steps, env changes).
